style_guide:
# Brand Positioning & Refresh Strategy

## Purpose

Create a strategic brand-refresh playbook that connects market change, audience psyche, cultural tension, positioning, value proposition, sensory identity, rollout, and measurable impact. It should guide decisions by brand, product, design, content, retail, and digital teams. It is not a logo reveal or mood board. Preview brand names, competitors, personas, materials, metrics, and quotations are fictional.

## Visual signature

Use a quiet, tactile editorial system built from alabaster linen, warm ochre, terracotta clay, and dark espresso. High-contrast serif headlines provide elegance; humanist sans-serif handles evidence and operating detail; small tracked labels organize sections. Pages use broad margins, fine warm rules, thin outlined panels, and occasional italic strategic statements. No glossy effects.

## Canvas and layout

- Fixed 16:9 canvas with `95–120 px` side margins and an 11- or 12-column grid.
- Reserve `145–185 px` for section index, serif title, and page count.
- Use balanced two-column comparisons, three equal insight cards, positioning-map plus value-proposition split, or three-phase roadmap.
- Keep the bottom `110–150 px` available for one italic strategic implication when needed.
- Corners are subtle under `5 px`; borders are one warm-gray pixel; shadows are prohibited.

## Colors

- Alabaster linen `#FAF8F5`: dominant canvas.
- Warm ochre `#9E7451`: primary structure, section labels, rules, and strategic emphasis.
- Terracotta clay `#D07B5A`: accent, selected position, phase highlight, and KPI delta.
- Dark espresso `#2C2520`: titles and primary ink.
- Soft parchment `#F1ECE5`: alternate panel fill.
- Warm gray `#756B62`: explanatory text.
- Hairline `#DED7CF`: dividers.
- These colors are identity colors, not performance semantics. Use explicit labels for KPI status.

## Typography

Use `Playfair Display`, `Georgia`, or `Source Serif 4` for titles, positioning statements, and strategic quotations. Use `IBM Plex Sans`, `Inter`, `Aptos`, or `Arial` for body and operating detail. Cover title `54–68 px`; body title `38–48 px`; card title `23–30 px`; large KPI `44–60 px`; body `13–17 px`; label `10–12 px` with restrained tracking.

## Persistent frame

Body pages begin with a numbered uppercase section label in ochre, followed by a large espresso serif title and thin horizontal rule. Page count sits upper right. When used, one italic strategic implication spans the lower margin and is paired with a small functional label such as Core Insight or Strategic Alignment.

## Page archetypes

### 1. Cover and strategic playbook

Use a split composition: left-side contents or chapter index and right-side title block. Include initiative, audience, document reference, release date, and confidentiality. Keep the cover calm and text-led.

### 2. Market shift and brand imperative

Use two large fields comparing legacy focus with the emerging paradigm. For each side show behavior, relationship, touchpoints, and evidence. End with a one-sentence strategic imperative that explains what must change.

### 3. Consumer tribe and cultural tension

Use three columns for audience archetype, cultural tension, and the brand's curated response. Each claim should trace to research. Avoid fictional persona details; emphasize motivations, context, behaviors, contradictions, and accessibility.

### 4. Positioning map and value proposition

Pair a labeled two-axis map with the core value proposition and two or three proof pillars. Define axes, sample, source, and competitor set. Positioning language must specify audience, frame of reference, differentiated value, and reason to believe.

### 5. Visual identity and communication system

Show typography, tone principles, core palette, materiality, image direction, and usage rules. Provide exact color values and accessibility constraints. This page defines principles, not a complete brand-guideline replacement.

### 6. Implementation roadmap and KPIs

Use three phases across a 12-month or appropriate horizon, each with decisions, deliverables, owners, channels, dependencies, and gates. Pair the roadmap with three metrics including baseline, target, method, owner, and review cadence.

## Brand-evidence integrity

Never invent consumer research, preference, competitor location, brand lift, conversion, referral, provenance, sustainability, or cultural resonance. Distinguish qualitative synthesis from measured fact. Define samples, markets, dates, and research methods. Validate color contrast, typography availability, localization, and production feasibility. Reconcile positioning, identity choices, rollout, and KPIs.

## Avoid

Do not use glossy gradients, generic lifestyle stock, logo walls, unexplained mood imagery, trend language without evidence, or decorative earth tones. Do not position competitors on arbitrary axes. Do not claim a refresh improved business outcomes before rollout and measurement.
